newsitem.title: USA: Ocean Spray seeks to close 2 bottling lines.
newsitem.headline: Ocean Spray seeks to close 2 bottling lines.

text.p: Ocean Spray Cranberries Inc, a marketing cooperative of cranberry and grapefruit growers, said on Wednesday that it plans to close bottling lines at its Markham, Wash., and Middleboro, Mass. plants to improve efficency.
About 315 jobs would be eliminated at the two plants under this plan, Ocean Spray spokesman John Lawlor said.

The company intends to inform the unions representing employees about its plans so they could offer alternatives to closing the bottling lines and work with employees to ease their transition into other jobs, Lawlor said.
Ocean Spray said the scaling back of its operations could begin as early as mid-autumn.
The Markham and Middleboro plants will continue to receive fruit and process it into juice or concentrate, as well as package fresh cranberries, Ocean Spray said in a statement.

Lawlor said operating costs and the age and location of the facilities weighed on Ocean Spray's plans to close the sites. Other Ocean Spray bottling lines will absorb the work that was done at the two plants, the company said.
The plan involves to loss of 165 of 236 current employees at the Markham plant and 150 of 321 employees at the Middleboro plant, Ocean Spray said.
Anticipated savings from the plan to close the bottling lines would be used to develop new products and markets, the company said.
